run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-16T14:33:44Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning for otel-demo/frontend is backed by real error-status spans on the frontend: in the hour ending 14:51:44 the frontend accumulated ~1963 error spans, concentrated on exactly two call paths — grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds (surfaced as GET /api/data) at ~407.7 spans/hour and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (surfaced as POST /api/checkout) at ~79.3 spans/hour, plus 15.25 tcp.connect errors. At 14:32:40–14:32:41 both the ad and payment Deployments were rollout-restarted (kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt; pod templates identical to the previous ReplicaSets in image, env and resources; revisions 1→2), and the old pods ad-554b849958-6z62j and payment-55766d76b9-9fxhp were stopped at 14:32:43/14:32:44. The frontend's error burst starts at 14:32:44 and runs to ~14:42:44, matching the interval in which ad's GetAds span count went to zero (zero for the 2-minute windows ending 14:35:44 through 14:41:44) and its request logging begins only at 14:40:28, and in which payment received no charges until 14:35:37. Neither dependency recorded a matching error-span burst, and both served successfully once requests arrived, so the failures came from calls not reaching the restarted pods rather than from the pods rejecting them. A contributing configuration fact: the ad, payment, frontend and checkout Deployments declare no readiness, liveness or startup probes, so the replacements were reported Ready 2–3 s after container start (ad 14:32:43, payment 14:32:44) under tight CPU limits (ad 50m, payment 20m). The ad Deployment is the dominant origin (~83% of frontend error spans, longest traffic gap); the payment Deployment is a second, independently evidenced contributor for the checkout segment. The frontend-proxy also recorded error spans on ingress (519.5/hour) and router frontend egress (487.0/hour), while cart, currency, product-catalog, shipping, email, quote, accounting and image-provider showed no error burst and recommendation/fraud-detection stayed at baseline. Two candidates were rejected: the flagd-config flags adFailure and paymentUnreachable (these would leave server-side error spans and traffic, not zero traffic), and the fraud-detection OOMKill at 14:34:27 (a Kafka-side consumer with no error burst).

claims.text: In the hour ending 14:51:44 the frontend produced ~1963 error-status spans, in exactly these series: GET (407.68), GET /api/data (407.68), executing api route (pages) /api/data (407.68), grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds (407.68), POST (79.3), POST /api/checkout (79.3), executing api route (pages) /api/checkout (79.3), grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (79.3) and tcp.connect (15.25). No error series existed for grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart or grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations.

checkout's own error-status spans were limited to oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and its client span oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge (79.88, 75.94 and 76.0 per 1-hour step), i.e. the failure was in the payment call made by checkout.
Neither payment nor ad recorded an error-status burst: payment's error-span increase was 0 at every sampled point in the window, and ad's was a low baseline (1.03 → 2.35 per hour).

Timing of the frontend error burst: the AdService path series were 0 up to 14:31:44, first nonzero at 14:33:44 (5.33 per 2 min), high from 14:35:44 (142.67) through 14:42:44 (35.53), then 0 from 14:43:44; the checkout/payment path series were nonzero only 14:32:44–14:36:44 (8, 8.88, 96, 37.33) and 0 from 14:37:44.

In the same interval the dependencies' own traffic dropped to zero: ad's oteldemo.AdService/GetAds span increase was 0 for the 2-minute windows ending 14:35:44, 14:37:44, 14:39:44 and 14:41:44 (nonzero 129.33 before and 149.33 at 14:43:44), and payment's charge/grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge span increase was 0 for the window ending 14:35:44.

The ad and payment Deployments were both rollout-restarted at 14:32:41 and 14:32:40 (template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt), moving from revision 1 to revision 2 with unchanged image (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad, …-payment), unchanged env, resources and labels; only the restartedAt annotation and pod-template-hash differ between the old and new ReplicaSets.

No other workload was restarted in that timeframe: ad (revision 2, restartedAt 14:32:41) and payment (revision 2, restartedAt 14:32:40) are the only Deployments with a restartedAt value there; flagd was restarted earlier at 14:01:50 and all other Deployments remain revision 1 with no restartedAt.

Kubernetes events show the old pods being stopped: 'Stopping container ad' for Pod/ad-554b849958-6z62j at 14:32:43 and 'Stopping container payment' for Pod/payment-55766d76b9-9fxhp at 14:32:44; the replacement pods are ad-5f8dd7c58d-rtbj5 (container started 14:32:43) and payment-5d565cf9b-8gwcn (started 14:32:44).
Both replacement pods reported Ready almost immediately: ad-5f8dd7c58d-rtbj5 Ready=True at 14:32:43 and payment-5d565cf9b-8gwcn Ready=True at 14:32:44, 2–3 seconds after container start.

The ad, payment, frontend and checkout Deployments declare no readinessProbe, livenessProbe or startupProbe at all, and their containers have tight CPU limits (ad 50m, payment 20m, frontend 100m, checkout 250m), so 'Ready' reflects only that the container process started.

The restarted ad container's request traffic resumed at about 14:40:28: its log stream read for 14:33:00–14:41:00 begins with 'Targeted ad request received for [..]' / 'Non-targeted ad request received…' lines at 14:40:28.774 and continues through 14:40:57.973, i.e. normal successful handling once requests arrived; this matches its GetAds span count of 0 through the window ending 14:41:44.

The restarted payment container's first post-restart log line is 14:35:37 ('Charge request received.' followed by 'Transaction complete.'), after which it processed a continuous stream of successful charges (e.g. the stream read from 14:39:32 onward shows every charge completed).
Errors reached the edge: frontend-proxy recorded error-status spans on its 'ingress' operation (519.56 per hour) and 'router frontend egress' operation (487.03 per hour) in the same hour.

Checked and without an error burst in the same hour: cart, currency, product-catalog, shipping, email, quote, accounting and image-provider returned only STATUS_CODE_UNSET/STATUS_CODE_OK series, and recommendation (4.07/hour) and fraud-detection (1.02/hour) stayed at their baseline error levels.

Changed during the window for another reason: the fraud-detection container was OOMKilled (lastState.terminated reason OOMKilled, exitCode 137, finishedAt 14:34:27) and restarted at 14:34:28 with restartCount 1; the pod is now Running and Ready.

The flagd-config ConfigMap currently declares adFailure defaultVariant 'on' and paymentUnreachable defaultVariant 'on' (all other faults 'off'); this is the ConfigMap's state at query time and not proof of what was served during the incident.

Jaeger's stored traces end at data_as_of 14:17:17, so no spans exist in the store for 14:32–14:43; the sampled traces from 14:17:16–14:17:17 show successful calls on these paths (frontend GET/POST http.status_code 200, frontend→ad grpc status 0, checkout→payment grpc status 0, payment 'charge' span present).

Most likely cause of the frontend alert: the rollout restart of the ad Deployment at 14:32:41 (and, in parallel, of the payment Deployment at 14:32:40) made the frontend's GetAds calls and checkout's PaymentService/Charge calls fail until the replacement containers actually began serving (~14:40:28 for ad, ~14:35:37 for payment). The frontend then returned errors on GET /api/data and POST /api/checkout, raising its request error rate above 0 and firing RequestErrorRate. Supporting signals: the error burst starts at 14:32:44 right after the old pods were stopped; ad and payment served zero requests during the burst (their own span series read 0); neither dependency emitted a matching error-span burst, so the calls did not reach them; both handled requests normally again once serving; no other service shows an error burst. The exact per-call error text (e.g. connection refused vs. DNS failure) could not be read because no spans exist for the burst interval.

Contributing factor to the length of the impact: because these Deployments define no readiness/startup probe, endpoints were populated as soon as the containers started (ad Ready at 14:32:43, payment at 14:32:44) while the applications were still starting under very small CPU limits (ad 50m, payment 20m), so callers were routed to not-yet-serving pods for minutes. The exact startup mechanics are inferred; the probe absence, CPU limits, Ready timestamps and the zero-traffic interval are observed directly.

Rejected as the cause of this burst: the flagd flags adFailure='on' and paymentUnreachable='on' in flagd-config. If they had been effective at the services, ad would have kept receiving GetAds calls and emitted error spans and payment would have rejected charges; instead ad's error-span count stayed at its ~2/hour baseline while its GetAds span count went to 0, and payment logged 'Transaction complete.' for the charges it did receive. What flagd actually served during the burst could not be verified.

Rejected as the cause of the frontend error rate: the fraud-detection OOMKill at 14:34:27. fraud-detection is not on the synchronous frontend request path in the sampled traces (checkout publishes to Kafka via an 'orders publish' span) and its own error-span rate stayed at 1.02/hour with no burst, so this restart does not explain errors on the frontend's GetAds and PaymentService/Charge calls.

The frontend, checkout and the replacement ad/payment pods did not crash: frontend-675fd7b5c5-68tcg, checkout-5dccddf8bb-vxwlj, ad-5f8dd7c58d-rtbj5 and payment-5d565cf9b-8gwcn all have restartCount 0 and are Running/Ready, so the error burst is not a crash-loop of the alerting service itself.

Before the restart the same call paths were healthy: traces sampled at 14:17:16–14:17:17 show frontend POST /api/checkout and GET /api/data with http.status_code 200, frontend→ad grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds status 0, checkout→payment grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge status 0, and the payment 'charge' internal span complete.

Add readiness and startup probes (and preferably minReadySeconds) to the ad and payment Deployments — and review frontend and checkout too — so that a rollout restart cannot publish endpoints for containers whose applications are not yet serving; consider maxUnavailable 0 and a larger CPU limit for the JVM-based ad container during startup.

Have a human reconcile the flagd-config state: it declares adFailure and paymentUnreachable 'on' while observed dependency behaviour contradicts those faults taking effect; confirm what flagd is actually serving and reset them if they are leftovers.

Investigate the fraud-detection memory limit separately: its container was OOMKilled (exit 137) at 14:34:27 and restarted; this is distinct from the frontend error rate but will recur without a memory-limit or leak fix.

gaps: No Prometheus alerting rule named RequestErrorRate (or any alerting rule) was returned — both rule queries came back no_data — so the alert's exact expression and the meaning of its 'current: 4.422222222222222' value are unknown; only trace-derived error signals could be checked.

Jaeger's stored traces stop at 14:17:17, so no span and no error tag/status detail exists for the 14:32–14:43 burst; the connection-level nature of the GetAds and PaymentService/Charge failures is inferred from the absence of server-side traffic and error spans, plus frontend tcp.connect error spans, not from read error text.

The frontend container's logs could not be read: both log reads returned no_data with 0 lines for the current and previous instance, so there is no application-log evidence from the alerting service itself.

The ad pod log read for 14:32:00–14:36:00 returned no_data (0 lines, with 218 lines outside that window dropped), so ad's log silence during the first minutes after its restart is not established; only the 14:33:00–14:41:00 read, which starts at 14:40:28, and the zero GetAds span counts support the traffic gap.

The flagd pod's log read returned no_data (0 lines for all containers) and flagd's effective in-memory flag set is not observable, so whether/when adFailure and paymentUnreachable were actually served during the window is unverified; change history is also unavailable because the change_history integration is not connected.

What or who issued the ad/payment rollout restarts at 14:32:40–14:32:41 is unknown, and the terminated pods' previous-container logs are no longer available (previous-instance reads returned unavailable).

The exact mechanism of the 3–8 minute no-traffic period (caller-side DNS/connection caching vs. slow application start behind a probe-less 'Ready') is not established; only probe absence, CPU limits, Ready timestamps and the zero-traffic interval are observed.

Service/endpoint state during the outage is unknown: only the current single-endpoint state of the ad and payment Services (each pointing at the new pod) could be read, and pod-level metric series (kube_pod_container_info) were not present in Prometheus.
next_steps: Inspect the change/deployment record (change_history integration is not connected here) to confirm who triggered the ad and payment rollout restarts at 14:32:40–14:32:41 and why.
Review ad and payment container start-up logs from their current instances for 14:32:43–14:40:28 to confirm when each application began serving.
Add readiness/startup probes to the demo Deployments (ad, payment, and review frontend/checkout) and validate that a rollout no longer produces client-visible errors.
Verify the effective flagd flag values for adFailure and paymentUnreachable and reset them if they are unintended.
Follow up on the fraud-detection OOMKilled restart at 14:34:27 as a separate reliability issue.

Before the restart the same call paths were healthy: traces sampled at 14:17:16–14:17:17 show frontend POST /api/checkout and GET /api/data with http.status_code 200, frontend→ad grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds status 0, checkout→payment grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge status 0, and the payment 'charge' internal span complete.

rejected_hypothesis.text: Rejected as the cause of this burst: the flagd flags adFailure='on' and paymentUnreachable='on' in flagd-config. If they had been effective at the services, ad would have kept receiving GetAds calls and emitted error spans and payment would have rejected charges; instead ad's error-span count stayed at its ~2/hour baseline while its GetAds span count went to 0, and payment logged 'Transaction complete.' for the charges it did receive. What flagd actually served during the burst could not be verified.

Rejected as the cause of the frontend error rate: the fraud-detection OOMKill at 14:34:27. fraud-detection is not on the synchronous frontend request path in the sampled traces (checkout publishes to Kafka via an 'orders publish' span) and its own error-span rate stayed at 1.02/hour with no burst, so this restart does not explain errors on the frontend's GetAds and PaymentService/Charge calls.
